purpose: Give the robot a machine-readable grammar for interpreting public-budget data without confusing planning, authorization, procurement, accounting execution, or policy outcomes.

methodological_reference.author: James Giacomoni
methodological_reference.title: Orcamento publico
methodological_reference.freshness_boundary: Methodological reference does not prove current law, current classifications, current thresholds, or empirical municipal facts. Current official normative and empirical sources must be checked separately.

knowledge_layers.role: Explains how to conceptualize and interpret public budgeting.
Defines the applicable legal and regulatory framework at a validated date.
Provides observed planning, authorization, procurement, accounting, contract, or payment facts.

core_concepts.definition: Political, legal, administrative and financial instrument through which government plans, authorizes, manages and controls public action.
core_concepts.interpretation: Budget data are not merely accounting numbers; they must be read together with objectives, programs, classifications, authorization and execution stages.

core_concepts.definition: Programming logic that relates public objectives to programs, actions, resources, products and expected results.
core_concepts.interpretation: Programmatic linkage can support planning correspondence but does not by itself prove that all program resources belong to a specific policy.

core_concepts.definition: Pluriannual planning instrument that organizes medium-term directions, objectives, programs, indicators and targets.
Annual planning-budget bridge that establishes priorities, guidelines and rules for preparation and execution of the annual budget.
Annual budget law that estimates revenues and fixes/authorizes expenditures for the fiscal year.

classification_dimensions.question: In what government function/subfunction is the spending classified?
For what objective/program/action is the resource planned or executed?
What economic kind of expenditure or revenue is it?

evidence_stages.note: Includes credits or changes when explicitly observed.
Can prove reporting totals/buckets within scope but not necessarily individual transaction identity.

interpretation_rules.rule: PPA planned values are planning intent and must not be relabelled as authorization or execution.
LOA appropriation is authorization, not proof of commitment, liquidation or payment.
PNCP procurement, homologation or contract evidence does not prove commitment, liquidation or payment.
Commitment, liquidation and payment are distinct evidence stages and cannot be substituted for one another.
A broad program can contain a policy without making the entire program budget policy-specific.
Matching program/action codes across planning and budget documents prove continuity only when source semantics are compatible; they do not alone prove policy-specific financial identity.
Equal or similar amounts across records are insufficient to prove that records are the same transaction or procurement.
Multi-year monetary comparison must be labelled nominal unless a documented deflator/base-date transformation is applied.
Codes or labels from different years are not assumed comparable until classification semantics are reconciled.
A zero in one bucket, source or period proves only that scoped observation; it cannot be generalized to total policy spending.
Planning, authorization or spending can indicate institutional materiality or priority signals but does not by itself prove quality, implementation success or policy effects.
Academic methodological references never override current official legal or source definitions; legal semantics require dated official authority.
Cross-source identity promotion requires stable administrative keys or an exact evidence bundle; thematic similarity, chronology and search snippets are insufficient.
Execution-rate calculations should prefer updated appropriation over initial appropriation when budget modifications are known and semantically compatible.
Cash/payment comparisons across years must account for restos a pagar when relevant; fiscal authorization/commitment timing and cash timing are not equivalent.
